items.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

ctx.x: Did things get better in the 60s with the Civil Rights movement and all that? Did it get better?

They were going good. They were going all right. They seemed to be going good because people seemed to be sensitive to these things, and the morale of people seemed to be picked up a little bit, and the Caucasian people seemed to have a feeling that wow, boy, that’s a drag. And then Reagan became president, and he messed everything up again and set it back fifty years. That thing hurt me when they named that airport after him, after he fired all those air controllers, now they’re going to name an airport after…
I take it you’re not a Republican.
